conditions.text: Core rule: a word in the 7th case that stands for a following element (a para-saptamī, i.e. a sat-/aupaśleṣika-saptamī naming a sound, suffix or word) makes the operation fall on the element BEFORE it, never on the one after it. It is a restricting rule (niyama): the locative alone could point either way.

quotes.quote: तस्मिन्निति सप्तम्यर्थनिर्देशे पूर्वस्यैव कार्यं भवति, नोत्तरस्य।
किं सत्सप्तमी ? किं वा गङ्गायां घोष इति वदौपश्लेषिकाधिकरणे सप्तमी ? इति ।

conditions.text: Immediacy: 'nirdiṣṭa' means the operation falls on the IMMEDIATELY preceding element — no intervening sound (time-gaps outside saṃhitā are not counted). So a 7th that names something which follows a different, intervening element (e.g. परस्मैपदेषु after sic) does not by 1.1.66 make the earlier element the kāryin.

quotes.quote: सप्तमीनिर्देशेन विधीयमानं कार्यं वर्णान्तरेणाव्यवहितस्य पूर्वस्य बोध्यम्
व्यवधानं चात्र वर्णकृतमेव निषिध्यते, नतु कालकृतम् ।

conditions.text: Only a 7th of a WORD-FORM, never of a meaning: a 7th naming a sense, a circumstance or a domain has no before/after relation and is outside 1.1.66.

quotes.quote: शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्। जनपदे अतिशायने इति।

conditions.text: Kinds of 7th that are NOT 1.1.66 (the commentaries contrast them with the para-saptamī): (a) viṣaya-saptamī — 'when X is in view', the operation happening before X exists (e.g. the 2.4.35 adhikāra आर्धधातुके); (b) nimitta-saptamī of 2.3.37 (bhāva-lakṣaṇa), e.g. क्ङिति in 1.1.5; (c) a 7th naming an elision (luk/lopa), which cannot follow anything.

quotes.quote: आर्धधातुकशब्दस्यार्धधातुकत्वमनेकप्रत्ययसाधारणं सामान्यमर्थः, तेन च पौर्वापर्यं न सम्भवति।

conditions.text: When a sūtra has both a 5th and a 7th, the 5th (1.1.67) prevails and turns the 7th into a 6th: the operation then falls on the 7th-named element itself (Mahābhāṣya examples: तास्यादिभ्यः लसार्वधातुके, गोतो णित्, रुदादिभ्यः सार्वधातुके, ईदासः, आमि सर्वनाम्नः सुट्, आण्नद्याः, याडापः, ङमो ह्रस्वादचि ङमुण्नित्यम्; PIS 71: डः सि धुट् by paratva).

quotes.quote: यत्र तु <<डः सि धुट्>> [[8.3.29]] इत्यादावुभयोरप्यचारितार्थ्यं तत्र <<तस्मिन्निति>> [[1.1.66]] सूत्रापेक्षया <<तस्मादित्युत्तरस्य>> [[1.1.67]] इत्यस्य परत्वात्तेनैव व्यवस्था।

conditions.text: The 7th must name an element whose PRECEDING neighbour is the kāryin. Where the 7th-named item is itself the recipient — iṭ, which is always the ārdhadhātuka suffix's own āgama — 1.1.66 is not what decides (it would put the iṭ on the root).

quotes.quote: आर्धधातुकस्येट् यावानिण् नाम स सर्व आर्धधातुकस्य भवतीति विज्ञेयम्
यदि ह्रङ्गस्य स्यात्, `एकाच उपदेशेऽनुदात्तात्`  [[7.2.10]]  इति प्रत्ययस्येट्प्रतिषेधोऽनर्थकः स्यात्

conditions.text: Scope: it applies even where there is no doubt (so an explicit 'पूर्व' in a sūtra does not rule it out); but by lakṣya it does not apply in कर्तृकर्मणोः कृति (2.3.65).

quotes.quote: एवं च महाविषयेयं भवति यदि सर्वत्र -  सन्देहविषये, अन्यत्र च प्रवर्तते।
लक्ष्यानुरोधेन क्वचिदेवंजातीयकेष्वस्याः परिभाषाया अप्रवृत्तिरिति 'श्नान्नलोप' इति सूत्रे भाष्ये प्रपञ्चितत्वात्

conditions.text: Ekādeśa (6.1.84ff.): the one substitute replaces both neighbours by the sūtra's own पूर्वपरयोः; the Mahābhāṣya reads that as showing 1.1.66 and 1.1.67 do not both apply at once. So 1.1.66's 'operation on the preceding only' does not straightforwardly describe these rules.

quotes.quote: अचीत्येषा सप्तमी आदिति पञ्चम्याः षष्ठीं प्रकल्पयिष्यति तस्मिन्निति निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य [[1.1.68]] इति ॥
एवं तर्हि सिद्धे सति यत्पूर्वपरग्रहणं करोति तज्ज्ञापयत्याचार्यः  -  नोभे युगपत्प्रकल्पिके भवत इति ।

VIS24.text: Viṣaya-saptamī: the 2.4.35 adhikāra आर्धधातुके is declared a viṣaya-saptamī, not a para-saptamī (substitution happens as soon as an ārdhadhātuka is intended, before it exists).

PARA.text: Para-saptamī of a following form; the operation falls on the element immediately before it.

VIS6150.text: Viṣaya-saptamī: Kāśikā and Nyāsa read ल्यपि here as 'when ल्यप् is in view', the ā-substitution being done in upadeśa before the suffix arises.

ARTHA.text: The 7th names a meaning/semantic condition, not a following word-form; the Mahābhāṣya on 1.1.66 restricts the rule to a 7th of a word (शब्दे), not of a meaning (अर्थे).

NIF.text: The carried 7th is not in force in this sūtra (the sūtra's own word replaces it, or it is impossible here).

P5.text: Pañcamī prevails: the sūtra also has a 5th, and the operation falls on the element named by the 7th itself, which follows the 5th (1.1.67).

DOMAIN6326.text: देवताद्वन्द्वे names the compound (Kāśikā: 'the dvandva of deity names — in it, when the uttarapada follows, the pūrvapada ...'); the following element is the uttarapada, not the dvandva.

MIXED.text: One compound word joins a following-form condition with a domain/meaning condition; only part of it is a para-saptamī.

PARA6446.text: Carried आर्धधातुके (6.4.46) qualifying a specific following suffix. Nyāsa on 6.4.46: generic ārdhadhātuka = viṣaya-saptamī, a particular ārdhadhātuka = para-saptamī; here a particular suffix follows.

P56463.text: In दीङो युडचि क्ङिति the युट् goes to the vowel-initial kṅit suffix after दीङ् (5th wins over the 7th) — Nyāsa and Tattvabodhinī.

P56401.text: In हुझल्भ्यो हेर्धिः the 5th हुझल्भ्यः turns the carried 7th (हलि) into a 6th qualifying हि; the kāryin is the following हि (Nyāsa, Mahābhāṣya on 6.4.101).

CONTAIN.text: The 7th names the word or position in which the kāryin itself lies, not an element following it.

DOMAIN.text: The 7th names the compound or setting in which both kāryin and nimitta stand (a domain), not an element following the kāryin.

VIS7189.text: Kāśikā glosses 'सर्वनामस्थाने परतः', but Padamañjarī says the upadeśivad-vacana implies सर्वनामस्थाने must be taken as a viṣaya-saptamī (कैति = इति, digitisation artefact).

QUAL72.text: परस्मैपदेषु (7.2.1) follows the sic, not the aṅga that takes vṛddhi; Kāśikā reads it as qualifying the sic ('परस्मैपदपरे सिचि'). By 1.1.66 with its adjacency the operation would fall on the sic.

IT.text: iṭ rules: the iṭ is an āgama of the ārdhadhātuka suffix itself (7.2.35, generalised by yoga-vibhāga), so the 7th names the suffix that receives (or is denied) the iṭ. By 1.1.66 the iṭ would fall on the preceding root.

P57283.text: Mahābhāṣya and Nyāsa: in ईदासः the 5th आसः makes the carried 7th आने a 6th — आन itself is replaced.

P57393.text: Nyāsa/Padamañjarī on 7.3.93 (ब्रुव ईट्): the 5th turns the carried 7th सार्वधातुके (with हलि, पिति, अपृक्ते) into a 6th — the ईट्/अट् goes to the following sārvadhātuka. Same in 7.3.94–100.

P57393Y.text: Nyāsa on 7.3.112 and Mahābhāṣya (याडापः): the 5th turns the carried ङिति into a 6th — the āgama goes to the following ङित् suffix.

NIP.text: Nipātana (ready-made forms); the source does not analyse the 7th as a rule-by-rule nimitta, so a 1.1.66 credit cannot be confirmed or refuted.

NIF7489.text: Kāśikā on 7.4.89 says explicitly that the carried यङ्यङ्लुकोः does not apply here.

QUAL.text: The 7th describes what follows the real nimitta, not the kāryin; because 1.1.66 requires immediate adjacency (निर्दिष्टग्रहणमानन्तर्यार्थम्), it would put the operation on the intervening element.

LOPA111.text: ढ्रलोपे: Kāśikā reads it as a bahuvrīhi ('that in which ḍh/r was elided') and the sūtra itself says पूर्वस्य, which Kāśikā gives its own purpose; and an elided sound cannot strictly 'follow' (Bālamanoramā on 7.3.89). Whether 1.1.66 has any role is unclear.

VISAYA.text: Viṣaya-saptamī (a domain: Veda, Mantra, Yajus, etc.), not a following form.

P56404.text: Mahābhāṣya on 6.4.104: the 5th चिणः turns the 7th क्ङिति into a 6th — the following suffix is elided.

P5HI.text: The हि named (via क्ङिति) is itself elided after the 5th; 1.1.67 governs.

KARYIN.text: The 7th qualifies the kāryin itself (what is replaced/elided), not a following nimitta.

DOMAIN7321.text: देवताद्वन्द्वे names the compound in which both members get vṛddhi (Kāśikā 7.3.21); it is a domain, not a following form.

SVARA.text: Accent rule where the accent does not plainly fall on the element before the 7th-named one.

NOT7.text: Not a locative of a following form (adverb such as अन्यतरस्याम् 'optionally', or a 1st-case word).

TADANTA.text: Kāśikā reads the 7th as 'the word ending in X' (tadanta); the accented syllable is inside that word, not before it.

WORDCLASS.text: The 7th names the following uttarapada/suffix by a class of words (Kāśikā '…-वाचिनि उत्तरपदे'); it is the only word in the sūtra naming the following element. The Mahābhāṣya allows a meaning-7th to be taken as the word expressing it.

KARYIN62U.text: In the 6.2.111ff. (उत्तरपदादिः) / 6.2.143ff. (अन्तः) sections the accent falls on the uttarapada itself; the 7th naming the uttarapada names the kāryin.

YOGA.text: The 7th names a syntactic connection or usage ('when connected with / when X is used'), not a following form.

VIS8137.text: Nyāsa on 8.1.37: पूजायाम् is a viṣaya-saptamī (a meaning).

LOPA.text: The 7th names an elision (lopa/luk/lup); an elided element is an absence and cannot stand after anything (Bālamanoramā, Nyāsa).

VIS1264.text: Nyāsa: एकविभक्तौ is a viṣaya- or sati-saptamī ('when one case-relation is intended'); ekaśeṣa is not an operation on a preceding element.

VIS2451.text: Bālamanoramā: the 7th in णौ च संश्चङोः (2.4.51) is a viṣaya-saptamī.

ANAIM.text: Tattvabodhinī: the ā-substitution is unconditioned (done in upadeśa); अशिति is a prasajya-pratiṣedha.

VIS8203.text: Tattvabodhinī and Bālamanoramā on 8.2.3: ने is a viṣaya-/sat-saptamī ('when the ना-substitution is to be done'); the rule is a non-asiddhatva statement, no operation on a preceding element.

MIXED8315.text: One compound word: खरि is a para-saptamī, अवसाने a viṣaya-saptamī (Kāśikā on 1.4.110; Padamañjarī on 8.3.15). Licensed for the khar half only.

VIS1410.text: Kāśikā (on 1.4.110): with respect to avasāna, the 7th is a viṣaya-saptamī, not a para-saptamī — a pause does not follow anything.

VIS6443.text: Kāśikā glosses 'यकारादौ ... परतः', but Tattvabodhinī calls ये in ये विभाषा a viṣaya-saptamī and Padamañjarī discusses both a viṣaya and a para reading.

VIS7317.text: Nyāsa on 7.3.17: संज्ञा cannot follow, so the 7th is a viṣaya-saptamī; and since one 7th cannot be both viṣaya and para, it is taken as viṣaya for शाण as well.

P58332.text: Paribhāṣenduśekhara 71: in ङमो ह्रस्वादचि ङमुण्नित्यम् the 7th अचि is used up in 8.3.33, so the 5th governs; ङमुट् goes to the following vowel.

VIS34103.text: Nyāsa on 3.4.103: परस्मैपदेषु is a viṣaya-saptamī, not a para-saptamī (the parasmaipada ending cannot follow the लिङ् — it IS the लिङ्).

P5AM.text: The आम् itself receives नुट् after the 5th; 1.1.67 governs (cf. Paribhāṣenduśekhara 71 on the parallel 7.1.52).

VIS7165.text: Nyāsa and Padamañjarī on 7.1.65: यि is a viṣaya-saptamī (नुम् comes before the y-initial suffix arises).

P58329.text: Paribhāṣenduśekhara 71 / Padamañjarī: in डः सि धुट् (and नश्च) neither case has other scope, so the later 1.1.67 decides; धुट् goes to the following स.

P56374.text: Tattvabodhinī on 6.3.74: as in डः सि धुट्, the 5th turns अचि into a 6th — नुट् goes to the vowel-initial uttarapada.

VIS7151.text: Nyāsa on 7.1.51: आत्मप्रीतौ is a viṣaya-saptamī (and a meaning).

P5PIS71.text: Paribhāṣenduśekhara 71: in आमि सर्वनाम्नः सुट् both the 7th (used up in 7.1.53) and the 5th (used up in 7.1.50) have scope, and the 5th wins by being later; the सुट् goes to the आम्. The Mahābhāṣya lists this sūtra.

P57276.text: Mahābhāṣya and Nyāsa: in रुदादिभ्यः सार्वधातुके the 5th wins; the iṭ goes to the sārvadhātuka.

LADESA.text: The 7th names the lakāra whose ending is being chosen (ātmanepada/parasmaipada replaces it), or a co-occurring element that stands BEFORE the ending; not a following nimitta.

STATE.text: The 7th names a stage of the derivation (non-causal / causal state), not a following form.

UPAPADA.text: An upapada (3.1.92) stands before the root, so its 7th is not a following nimitta.

VIS4190.text: Mahābhāṣya on 4.1.90: अचि (from 4.1.89) is a viṣaya-saptamī, not a para-saptamī.

EKADESA.text: Ekādeśa: the single substitute replaces BOTH the preceding element and the 7th-named following one, by 6.1.84 पूर्वपरयोः. The Mahābhāṣya notes 1.1.66/1.1.67 would each give one sthānin, and reads the explicit पूर्वपरग्रहण as showing they do not both apply at once. The 7th is positionally a para-saptamī, but 1.1.66's 'operation on the preceding only' is not what happens.

VIS12.text: In 1.2.11–17 the ātmanepada ending follows सिच् but REPLACES लिङ् (so for लिङ् it is not a following element); Kāśikā writes 'आत्मनेपदेषु परतः', the prathamāvṛtti writes 'आत्मनेपदविषये' for several of these sūtras. Licensed for sic, doubtful for liṅ.

PARA6462.text: Licensed for the ciṇvad-bhāva of the aṅga before स्य etc.; the iṭ of the same sūtra goes to स्य etc. themselves (Mahābhāṣya: yoga-vibhāga of 7.2.35).

VIS6462.text: Padamañjarī: भावकर्मणोः is a viṣaya-saptamī (वषय = विषय, artefact). The Mahābhāṣya does try a 1.1.66 reading (the meaning taken as the word bearing it) before settling on a yoga-vibhāga.

NIMITTA.text: A nimitta-saptamī (2.3.37 bhāva-lakṣaṇa), which the Nyāsa (on 1.1.5) says is NOT governed by 1.1.66.

EXC6523.text: Bālamanoramā on 1.1.66: in कर्तृकर्मणोः कृति 1.1.66 does not apply (the genitive occurs whether the kṛdanta follows or precedes), on the authority of the Mahābhāṣya on 6.4.23.

MENTION.text: Layer-1 credit: the commentator applies 1.1.66 to a different sūtra discussed in passing.

AGAINST.text: Layer-1 credit whose quoted commentary says 1.1.66 does NOT apply here (or explains why the sūtra avoids a 7th).

P57190.text: Mahābhāṣya: in गोतो णित् the 5th गोतः turns the carried 7th सर्वनामस्थाने into a 6th; the ending after गो is णित्.

P57190B.text: As in 7.1.90: the 5th सख्युः makes the following सर्वनामस्थान the kāryin (Kāśikā 'तस्मात् परं सर्वनामस्थानं णिद् भवति').

VIS3131.text: Kāśikā/Nyāsa on 3.1.31: आर्धधातुके is a viṣaya-saptamī ('when an ārdhadhātuka is intended').

VIS4122.text: Nyāsa on 4.1.22: तद्धितलुकि is a viṣaya-saptamī; an elision cannot stand after anything.

VIS4131.text: Nyāsa on 4.1.31: अजसौ is a viṣaya-saptamī, not a para-saptamī.

VIS1104.text: Siddhānta-kaumudī on 1.1.4: आर्धधातुके is a viṣaya-saptamī.

NIMITTA115.text: Nyāsa on 1.1.5: क्ङिति is a nimitta-saptamī (2.3.37), precisely so that the prohibition reaches non-adjacent guṇa/vṛddhi; 1.1.66 does not apply to it.

META.text: Layer-1 credit for a meta-statement; the sūtra itself has no 7th-case nimitta.

groups.group: carried / not a sūtra word | ādeśa | X: 7th case (carried over)
groups.how_checked: All 361 members read one by one (sūtra text, the word's case/anuvṛtti source, and the Kāśikā/prathamāvṛtti wording around the word); then scripted cross-checks over the whole set: (1) members whose sūtra also has a 5th-case word were listed and read for the 1.1.67 override; (2) carried words were checked against the Kāśikā gloss to see if they are actually in force; (3) commentator statements calling a 7th viṣaya-/nimitta-saptamī were searched in all eight commentaries.

unsure.why: Ekādeśa: the single substitute replaces BOTH the preceding element and the 7th-named following one, by 6.1.84 पूर्वपरयोः. The Mahābhāṣya notes 1.1.66/1.1.67 would each give one sthānin, and reads the explicit पूर्वपरग्रहण as showing they do not both apply at once. The 7th is positionally a para-saptamī, but 1.1.66's 'operation on the preceding only' is not what happens.
